subject.title: Feature: configurable bootstrap file injection order for prompt cache optimization

question: Should OpenClaw add a core typed config for per-file bootstrap dynamic classification/order, extend a plugin/context-engine API for this, or keep the current fixed ordering policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines a public prompt-cache and config contract in an area where repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces.

options.title: Add narrow dynamic-file config
options.body: Add a constrained `bootstrapDynamicFiles`-style core config with deterministic ordering, docs, schema/help, and tests, while deferring full arbitrary prompt layout control.

options.title: Expose plugin/context-engine control
options.body: Add or document the minimal extension seam needed for external packages to classify or reorder bootstrap files before prompt assembly without a broad core config knob.

options.title: Keep fixed core ordering
options.body: Decline new per-file ordering config and direct operators to existing `contextInjection`, bootstrap size limits, and workspace-file hygiene guidance.

recommendation.title: Add narrow dynamic-file config
recommendation.body: Add a constrained `bootstrapDynamicFiles`-style core config with deterministic ordering, docs, schema/help, and tests, while deferring full arbitrary prompt layout control.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears in recent prompt/config history and is the best available routing candidate for the core-config versus extension-boundary product choice.
